la:noun:comes.html:
cŏm-ĕs, ĭtis, comm.
con and 1. eo
(lit. one who goes with another),
a companion, an associate, comrade, partaker, sharer, partner, etc. (whether male or female; class. and freq.).
In gen.
Masc.: age, age, argentum numera, ne comites morer,: confugere domum sine comite,: comes meus fuit, et omnium itinerum meorum socius,: erat comes ejus Rubrius,: cui tu me comitem putas esse,: ibimus, o socii comitesque,; ; : Catulli,: Pisonis,; : quin et avo comitem sese Mavortius addet Romulus,; cf.: comes ire alicui,: comitem aliquem mittere alicui,: comes esse alicui, et saep. —
With gen. or dat. of thing: cum se victoriae Pompeji comitem esse mallet quam, etc.,: comitem illius furoris,: me tuarum actionum, sententiarum, etc., socium comitemque habebis,: mortis et funeris atri,: tantae virtutis,: exsilii,: fugae,; ; ; cf. : me habuisti comitem consiliis tuis,.—With in: comes in ulciscendis quibusdam,.—
Fem., ; : data sum comes inculpata Minervae,; cf. : me tibi venturam comitem,; ; .—
Transf. to inanimate objects: malis erat angor Assidue comes,: comes formidinis, aura,: ploratus mortis comites,: tunc vitae socia virtus, mortis comes gloria fuisset, (17, 39): multarum deliciarum comes est extrema saltatio,: pacis est comes, otiique socia eloquentia,; cf. an idea (perh. intentionally) opp. to this,: non ut ullam artem doctrinamve contemneres, sed ut omnis comites ac ministratrices oratoris esse diceres,: cui ipsi casus eventusque rerum non duces sed comites consiliorum fuerunt,: exanimatio. quas comes pavoris,: (grammatice) dulcis secretorum comes,: (cura) comes atra premit sequiturque fugacem,: culpam poena premit comes,: nec (fides) comitem abnegat,: comitemque

aeris alieni atque litis esse miseriam, Orac. ap. .—

In partic.
An overseer, tutor, teacher, etc., of young persons (rare; not ante-Aug.),; ; ; .— Esp. = paedagogus, a slave who accompanied boys as a protector, ; .—Far more freq.,
The suite, retinue of friends, relatives, scholars, noble youth, etc., which accompanied magistrates into the provinces, sq; ; ; ; ; .—
The attendants of distinguished private individuals, ; ; ; .—Trop.: (Cicero) in libris de Republica Platonis se comitem profitetur, Plin. praef. § 22.—
After the time of the emperors, the imperial train, the courtiers, court, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; —Hence,
In late Lat., a designation for the occupant of any state office, as, comes scholarum, rei militaris, aerarii utriusque, commerciorum (hence, Ital. conte; Fr. comte).

la:verb:comedo.html:
cŏm-ĕdo, ēdi, ēsum (comessum, Prol. ad Plaut. p 102 Ritschl), or estum, 3, v. a. (comesus, the more usual form, ; Varr R. R. 1, 2, 11; , Juv 1, 34; Valgius ap. P—Hence, comessurus, :
comestus,; , acc. to ; and , ext. 6, and Didius ap. Diom. l. l.—Contr forms: comes,: comest,; , ; Lucil, Titin., Afran., Varr., Cic. Hortens. ap. Non p. 81, 9 sq., comestis,: comesse,; , ; ; ; : comesses,: comesset,, : comesto,.—Old forms: comedim,; ; ap. comedis, : comedint,), to eat entirely up, to eat, consume (class.; esp. freq. in Plaut.).
Prop.: ubi oleae comesae erunt,: ubi daps profanata comestaque erit,: quod bibit, quod comest,: corbitam cibi Comesse possunt,: quid comedent?: celerius potuit (venenum) comestum quam epotum in venas permanare?: ex se enim natos comesse fingitur solitus (Saturnus),: quorum Dentes vel silicem comesse possunt. : haec porcis hodie comedenda relinques,: te muscae comedissent, Sicinius ap. ; and ap. : panem, Afer ap. .—Facetiously: lacertum Largii, Crass. ap. .—
Prov.: tam facile vinces quam pirum volpes comest,; and: cenà comesā venire, i. e. to come too late; post festum, a day after the fair, .—
Trop.: comedere aliquem oculis, to devour with one's eyes, i. e. to long eagerly for, : se, to consume one's self (by grief, sorrow, etc.), to waste or pine away, ; so Cic. Hortens. Fragm. ap. . —
Meton., to waste, dissipate, spend, squander: comedunt quod habent,; cf.: aurum in lustris,. meam dotem comest, Titin. ap. : paternam pecuniam, Novius ap. : nummos,: cura ut valeas, ne ego te jacente bona tua comedim,: beneficia Caesaris,: patrimonium,; : rem (sc. familiarem),: bona,; ; id. Fragm. ap. ; : cantherium,i. e. its value in money,.— Hence,
Transf. in the lang. of comedy: comedere aliquem, to waste or consume the property of any person, ; ; ; .
